newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks seen trendless, eyes on U.S. rates.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks seen trendless, eyes on U.S. rates.

text.p: Brazilian stocks may open mixed to lower Monday as investors keep a watchful eye on U.S. interest rates amid concerns about a large July trade gap, a probe into several brokerages, and declining foreign markets, brokers said.
"Markets worldwide are down. I think Brazil may follow suit," said John Carioba of Indusval brokerage. The market may follow through on Friday's downward trend at the open, he said.
The Sao Paulo bolsa's Bovespa index of 47 leading shares plunged 4.76 percent Friday to close at 12,259 on trading volume of 823.8 million reais ($761 million).
"I think the market today should continue to see a little fall," a local trader said.
The market also should see rising volatility as speculation mounts ahead of August 13 futures expiration and August 18 options settlements, brokers said.
